newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum prices may rise to $2,000/tonne - Spector.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum prices may rise to $2,000/tonne - Spector.

text.p: Aluminum prices this year could rise to $2,000 per tonne with Western World demand increasing by nearly six percent, industry analyst Stewart Spector said in his Aluminum Industry Service report.
Spector said his demand and price outlooks were much higher than industry consensus because other forecasters were using too low a base figure for Western world ingot shipments in 1995 and 1996.
"They were using roughly 17.5 million tons for both years, and we're using approximately 18.5 million tons," he said.
Using a different base, the additional demand under Spector's forecast equates to an extra 400,000 tons or 40 percent of total year end inventories in LME.
"A good part of the year-to-year gain comes from the completion of end-user destocking, and some modest growth in the underlying demand for ingot in a growing world economy," Spector said.
He added that his supply/demand scenario for 1997 makes it necessary for all idle Western smelter to be back in production in the last half of the year.

Supply may also be constrained by the lack of petroleum coke used in aluminum production, a possible inability of Commonwealth of Independent States and Eastern European smelters to get enough alumina once Western smelters were operating at full capacity, and a lack of new capacity being built between now and the turn of the century.
